title: Inactive beta1-integrin acts as a junctional scaffold for angiopoietin/TIE2/FOXO1 signaling.
authors: Sipila, Tuomas; Ponna, Srinivas Kumar; Venkatesha Murthy, Abhinandan; Pink, Anne; Enkavi, Giray; Bohra, Shraman Kumar; Lewna, Klaudia; Ganesh, Keerthana; Liu, Qina; Korhonen, Mirka; Kajander, Tommi; Potente, Michael; Ivaska, Johanna; Vattulainen, Ilpo; Leppanen, Veli-Matti; Saharinen, Pipsa
one_liner_zh: 该文通过MD模拟和晶体学解析ANGPT2与TIE2及整合素复合物结构，但核心是整合素-生长因子信号通路，非TF-DNA互作，仅方法可部分借鉴。
abstract: The blood and lymphatic vascular systems are regulated by angiopoietin (ANGPT) growth factors, which signal via endothelial TIE receptor tyrosine kinases and integrins. However, mechanistic understanding of how these receptors crosstalk is limited. Here, we show how beta1-integrin inactivation regulates endothelial ANGPT/TIE2 signaling. By integrating biophysical analyses, X-ray crystallography, size-exclusion chromatography-small-angle X-ray scattering and atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, we show that ANGPT2 binds through its asymmetrically positioned C-terminal fibrinogen-like domains to both TIE2 and alpha5beta1-integrin, forming a trimeric complex compatible with the inactive alpha5beta1-integrin conformation. Inactive beta1-integrin colocalizes with ANGPT-induced TIE2 in cell-cell junctions and stabilizing beta1-integrin in its inactive state enhances junctional TIE2 accumulation and promotes nuclear exclusion of the TIE2 transcriptional effector FOXO1 in cultured endothelial cells. Endothelial-specific beta1-integrin deletion in adult mice reduces venous TIE2 phosphorylation, whereas endotoxemia diminishes junctional beta1-integrin along with decreased phosphorylated TIE2. In contrast, without TIE2, ANGPT2 uniquely engages active beta1-integrin, via its N-terminal superclustering domain. Altogether, our results provide structural and mechanistic evidence of ANGPT signaling via alpha5beta1-integrin and support a model in which inactive alpha5beta1-integrin acts as a junctional scaffold for ANGPT/TIE2/FOXO1 signaling, explaining how integrin conformational switching spatially organizes growth factor signaling in the endothelium.
abstract_zh: 血液和淋巴血管系统受血管生成素（ANGPT）生长因子调控，这些因子通过内皮TIE受体酪氨酸激酶和整合素传递信号。然而，关于这些受体如何相互作用的机制理解仍然有限。在此，我们展示了β1-整合素失活如何调控内皮ANGPT/TIE2信号传导。通过整合生物物理分析、X射线晶体学、尺寸排阻色谱-小角X射线散射和原子级分子动力学模拟，我们表明ANGPT2通过其不对称定位的C端纤维蛋白原样结构域同时结合TIE2和α5β1-整合素，形成与失活α5β1-整合素构象兼容的三聚体复合物。失活的β1-整合素与ANGPT诱导的TIE2在细胞间连接处共定位，并且将β1-整合素稳定在失活状态可增强连接处TIE2的积累，并促进培养内皮细胞中TIE2转录效应因子FOXO1的核排斥。成年小鼠中内皮特异性β1-整合素缺失会降低静脉TIE2磷酸化，而内毒素血症则减少连接处β1-整合素并伴随磷酸化TIE2的降低。相反，在没有TIE2的情况下，ANGPT2通过其N端超聚集结构域独特地结合活性β1-整合素。总体而言，我们的结果提供了ANGPT通过α5β1-整合素信号传导的结构和机制证据，并支持一个模型，其中失活的α5β1-整合素作为ANGPT/TIE2/FOXO1信号传导的连接支架，解释了整合素构象转换如何空间组织内皮中的生长因子信号传导。
